title: PatternPaint: Practical Layout Pattern Generation Using Diffusion-Based Inpainting
problem: VLSI layout pattern generation requires large, design-rule-compliant training datasets; new technology nodes lack such data, making existing training-based methods impractical.
motivation: Design rules evolve with each new node; agile pattern generation enables rapid technology development.
method: PatternPaint fine-tunes a pretrained image model for chip layout generation using diffusion-based inpainting, a technique that fills in masked (hidden) parts of images by gradually removing noise. The method treats layout generation as an inpainting problem, handled through template-based denoising. Fine-tuning requires only 20 design-rule-compliant sample layouts, enabling it to work with new technology nodes that lack large training datasets.
key_novelty: PatternPaint adapts image-generation techniques (diffusion inpainting) to chip layout design, requiring only 20 example patterns instead of the thousands needed by existing methods.
contributions: Diffusion-based inpainting framework for layout patterns
Few-shot fine-tuning (20 samples) on pretrained models
Only framework generating legal patterns for Intel 18A (sub-3nm)
limitations: Evaluation limited to sub-3nm nodes; generalization to older technology nodes and other foundries not explored.
